Restrict to its equatorial plane, as in the Statement. [F1, F4, F5, A1]

Substituting $\theta=\pi/2$, $\dot\theta=0$ and these constants into $g(\gamma',\gamma')=0$ gives
$$-f\dot x^{0,2}+f^{-1}\dot r^2+r^2\dot\phi^2=0.$$
Multiplying by $f>0$ and using $\mathcal E=f\dot x^0$, $\ell=r^2\dot\phi$ yields $\dot r^2=\mathcal E^2-f\ell^2/r^2$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

The metric-selected Christoffel formula from [F3] gives $\Gamma^r{}_{00}=ff'/2$ and $\Gamma^r{}_{\phi\phi}=-fr$ on the equator. At a circular point, $\dot r=\ddot r=0$ and the radial geodesic equation becomes $ff'\dot x^{0,2}/2-fr\dot\phi^2=0$. The null condition gives $f\dot x^{0,2}=r^2\dot\phi^2$, so the radial equation is equivalent to
$$V'(r)=\frac{f'}{r^2}-\frac{2f}{r^3}=0.$$
Conversely, at an equatorial point with $f>0$ and $V'=0$, the same connection coefficients make the radial equation hold for the null circular tangent; the $x^0$ and $\phi$ equations have only terms proportional to $\dot r$, and the $\theta$ equation vanishes at $\theta=\pi/2$ by reflection symmetry. Thus solving $V'=0$ is necessary and sufficient for an equatorial circular null geodesic in the static region. [F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

Expanding $V=r^{-2}-2Mr^{-3}+Q^2r^{-4}$ gives
$$V'(r)=-\frac{2}{r^5}(r^2-3Mr+2Q^2).$$
The discriminant is $9M^2-8Q^2\ge M^2>0$, so its real roots are $r_\gamma^\pm=(3M\pm\sqrt{9M^2-8Q^2})/2$. Set $x=\sqrt{M^2-Q^2}\in[0,M]$ and $s=\sqrt{M^2+8x^2}=\sqrt{9M^2-8Q^2}$. Then
$$r_\gamma^+-r_+=\frac{M+s-2x}{2}>0,$$
because $s^2-(2x)^2=M^2+4x^2>0$, while
$$r_\gamma^--r_+=\frac{M-s-2x}{2}\le0$$

At $r=r_\gamma^+$ choose any $\ell\ne0$ and set $\mathcal E=|\ell|\sqrt{f(r_\gamma^+)}/r_\gamma^+>0$. Then the null condition and $V'(r_\gamma^+)=0$ make the radial geodesic equation hold with constant $r$. Taking $\dot x^0=\mathcal E/f>0$ and $\dot\phi=\ell/r^2$ makes the tangent nonzero and null; its pairing with the selected future timelike static field $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ is $g(\xi,\gamma')=-\mathcal E<0$, so [F6] makes it future-directed.
